advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile `_rereduce`'s doc/comment with its code: either fall back to the pass-one state on an error-dict re-reduce, or update the wording to say only a `None` reduce keeps the pass-one state.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:615: `    return full if isinstance(full, dict) else state`

Docstring at :609 and the comment at :595 ('A row that fails to re-reduce keeps its pass-one state rather than vanishing') claim the pass-one state is kept, but an error dict is a dict and is returned instead.
advisory.finding: `_rereduce`'s docstring says a row that fails to re-reduce "keeps its pass-one state rather than vanishing," but `reduce_ticket` returning a `reducer_failed`/`error` dict satisfies `isinstance(full, dict)`, so the error dict is returned and fed to `public_state` instead of the pass-one projected state. Only a `None` return falls back to the pass-one state.
scenarios: A session_log ticket reduces to type session_log in pass one but, on the per-ticket re-reduce, yields an error dict (e.g. cache/race/corruption) — the returned row becomes the error dict's public_state, not the 3-field pass-one row.
